content.value_statement: Managing many projects creates hidden dependencies and resource conflicts. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan roadmaps, allocation, and portfolio health.
actual_capabilities: Identifies cross-project dependencies and recommends coordination steps.
Builds quarterly, annual, theme-based, and initiative-based roadmap structures.
Compares dedicated, pooled, and matrix resource allocation models.
Creates portfolio health summaries with risks, utilization, and next actions.
Guides coordinated release workflows across multiple projects.
limitations: It depends on access to repositories, GitHub data, or user-provided project status.
It provides planning guidance and examples, not automatic project management enforcement.
Referenced template and script files may not be included in the installed package.
Shell examples should be reviewed before use in large or sensitive workspaces.

use_cases.title: Plan a Project Portfolio
use_cases.description: Create a portfolio roadmap that connects active projects to objectives, milestones, dependencies, and staffing needs.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Cross-Team Releases
use_cases.description: Sequence related releases, surface blockers, and define communication checkpoints across several delivery teams.

use_cases.title: Balance Shared Capacity
use_cases.description: Compare allocation options and choose a staffing model that reduces overload while preserving strategic progress.

prompt_templates.title: Map Current Projects
prompt_templates.prompt: List my active projects, summarize their goals, and identify likely dependencies, blockers, and missing status information.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Quarterly Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a quarterly roadmap for these projects. Include objectives, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Resource Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these staffing constraints and recommend a resource allocation plan across projects. Explain tradeoffs and escalation points.

prompt_templates.title: Design Portfolio Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-project governance model with decision rights, dependency tracking, health metrics, release coordination, and stakeholder reporting.

output_examples.input: We have four teams, six projects, and two shared platform dependencies.
output_examples.output: A portfolio roadmap with project priorities, dependency owners, release windows, staffing risks, and weekly coordination checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Two high-priority initiatives need the same senior engineers next quarter.
output_examples.output: A capacity recommendation comparing dedicated, pooled, and matrix allocation options with risks, benefits, and a preferred plan.

output_examples.input: Leadership needs a concise portfolio health update before planning review.
output_examples.output: An executive summary covering status, top risks, resource utilization, upcoming milestones, and decisions needed.

best_practices: Define project goals, owners, dependencies, and decision points before building the roadmap.
Review portfolio health on a regular cadence and update plans when assumptions change.
Keep resource allocation below full utilization so teams can handle unknown work.
anti_patterns: Do not create roadmaps without validating team capacity and dependency owners.
Do not treat every project as equal priority when resources are constrained.
Do not run broad workspace discovery commands without user-approved scope.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate project portfolios, cross-project dependencies, roadmap planning, resource allocation, releases, and portfolio health reporting.

faq.question: Can it manage projects automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured planning guidance and examples, while users still approve actions and maintain their project systems.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub access?
faq.answer: No, but GitHub access can improve project discovery when users want repository and issue data included.

faq.question: Can it support non-engineering projects?
faq.answer: Yes, but the examples are optimized for software teams, repositories, dependencies, releases, and engineering capacity.

faq.question: How should teams use the roadmap outputs?
faq.answer: Use them as planning drafts, then validate owners, timelines, risks, and priorities with stakeholders before execution.

faq.question: Is it safe to use in sensitive repositories?
faq.answer: Review command examples before running them and limit discovery to approved directories, organizations, and project data.
